Replies.Text:
**Build log** (agent session, Claude Fable 5.1). 183 tests pass (`node --test`).

**What was built**
- **Build button** (`public/js/build.js`, header): shown to the owner when the project has a workspace; disabled, with the reason as its hint, until the workspace has Build settings on an online worker, every thread is applied (the build's own aside) and nothing runs for the plan; **Build again** after a send-back. Its dialog picks the worker's claude-cli item and a model; Build sets the plan to Working and opens the panel on the run log.
- **Consensus's side** (`src/Api.js`, `src/Llm.js`): `POST /api/proposals/<id>/build`; `BuildPrompt` (implement only what the plan says, in the workspace as it is, run the tests, do nothing with git, open a thread for a reading taken or a point not built), `BUILD_SCHEMA`, `ParseBuild`. The answer's threads are opened (a bad anchor falls back to the whole plan, saying so), then the **build log** is posted as the contested whole-document receipt (job, worker, workspace, model, tokens, the log, the threads opened). **Resolve** accepts: applied outcome-only, the build's context written, the plan Finished, the worker told. **Reply** sends it back: Build again carries the last log and the reply, and the new log is a reply on the same thread (a round with no context keeps the earlier one). A failed build is said in the run log, and as a reply on a sent-back log. Reviews leave build logs alone.
- **The worker's side** (`src/Worker.js`): claude -p in the workspace's Root with Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, and Bash for `Build.Commands` only; `--restricted`, dontAsk; Exclude denied for Read and Edit; the commands listed at the end of the prompt. `Build: { Remote, Commands }` validated. No git on its own.
- **Commit and Push** on the worker's page, on an accepted build, pressed by you, queued and run in order: `git add -A` + one commit on the checked-out branch titled after the plan with the build log below, no trailers; Push the checked-out branch to Remote. Each result on the page and in the plan's run log.

**Found live, and fixed**: with the real claude -p, `git status` ran in a build although only `node --test` was allowed: claude lets some read-only commands through on its own. A PreToolUse hook now holds Bash to the commands (`bin/worker.js --bash-guard`, `BashAllowed`): an allowed command with arguments, nothing chained, piped, redirected or substituted. Run again live: `git status` refused, `private/secret.txt` (excluded) refused, `math.js` and `math.test.js` written, `node --test` passed, HEAD unchanged, no branch.

**How it was checked**
- `test/Workers.test.js`: when Build can run, the job and its prompt, the log and the build's threads, send back and build again, accept (applied, context, Finished, worker told), failures. `test/Worker.test.js`: a build in a scratch git repo with a stand-in claude (files changed in place, HEAD unmoved, no branch; Commit refused until accepted; then Commit and Push to a local bare repo), the Bash guard. `test/Ui.test.js`: the Build button and dialog.
